newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll shows 39 pct support for Canada's Liberals.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows 39 pct support for Canada's Liberals.

text.p: Canada's Liberal party is poised to return to goverment with its parliamentary majority intact and will face a Reform opposition, a poll published on Friday by the Toronto Globe and Mail newspaper showed.

The poll, conducted by Environics Research Group for Canada's influential daily newspaper, showed support for the Liberals among decided voters at 39 percent, compared with 20 percent for the Conservatives and 19 percent for right-wing Reform. The New Democrats received the support of 11 percent of decided voters, while 9 percent supported the separatist Bloc Quebecois.

A computerized projection by the newspaper on a riding-by-riding basis showed the Liberals would win 179 seats, Reform 55 seats and thus the official opposition, the Bloc 42 seats, Conservatives 16 and the New Democrats 9.
The poll of 1,852 voters was conducted from May 25 to May 28 and has a margin of error of 2.3 percent 19 times out of 20.

If the poll's results are sustained in Monday's general election, there will have been very little change since 1993 in overall party-support levels other than a small gain by the Conservatives at the expense of the Bloc and a modest increase in NDP support at the expense of the Liberals, the Globe said.
